Because its logical.


P.S, EDIT:
I am well aware that we may acces the information of the tile SourceID and altas coordinates via map.GetCellSourceId and GetCellAtlasCoords respectively.

I am just thinking that instead of me having 3 lines of code (so GetTileData, GetSourceID and GetCellAtlasCoords) it might be smart to add the information additionaly to the TileData object as well. Then this object would contain all information (at least with regards to the tileLayer in question).

I dont think existing methods  GetSourceID and GetCellAtlasCoords should be replaced or terminated, just that it might be beneficial to add this information to TileData as well - at least if the information is already known and present to the tiledata object itself internally.
answers.workaround:
I believe this infomation is crucial. You cannot have a valid tileData object without ID and Vector2 (position in the atlas).

Tile is defined by this information, its core to its identity.

However we may get the inforamtion relatively easily by using  tileMap.GetSourceID() and GetCellAtlasCoords().

title: TileData should expose information about Source/Atlas ID (int) and AtlasCoordinates (Vector2)
